lessons: Keep hooks concise and direct: the top-performing video ('Why Tuna Meat Is Red Meat While Cod Is Pure White') used an immediate, striking contrast at 8% into the video that retained an impressive 0.57 start metric.

Eliminate empty filler lines early: videos with vague hook lines or placeholder text (e.g., 'Why your eyes are secretly leaking') suffered early drop-offs exceeding 13% within the first 15% of the runtime.

Avoid redundant explanations: 'Why Highway Guardrails Have Heavy End Boxes' repeated the exact same line ('Instead of impaling your vehicle...') for consecutive drop points, resulting in poor end-retention (0.125).

Rethink pauses and countdowns: elements involving explicit pauses or countdown timers (e.g., in 'How 400 Degree Foil Stays Safe' and 'Why Car Windshields Have Black Dots') frequently coincided with the biggest viewer drop-off points.

Incorporate rare, extreme natural facts: the 'This Shark Can Live For Centuries!' video leveraged a uniquely extreme premise ('older than the United States'), achieving massive rewatch metrics (1.85 at 10%, 1.08 at end).
worst_moment_types: Vague filler statements (e.g., 'They are not just there to look cool')
Slow-paced pauses or countdown mechanics (e.g., 'Pause and guess... three, two, one')
best_hook_types: Immediate startling contrasts or biological oddities (e.g., fish meat comparisons, extreme lifespans)
Direct, high-stakes physical phenomena tied to everyday objects
Action-driven physical danger or bodily reactions (spicy food, shark aging, fresh pineapple enzymes)
